Documentation → Monitoring & Analysis → Backend Reachability

Backend Reachability (batch)

Paste or upload a list of source;policy;destination lines and SATOM checks, per line, whether the real servers behind each FortiWeb server policy answer — on the source box and then on the destination box — without writing anything.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view
📍 WhereOperations → Troubleshooting → Backend Reachability (the Global block in the Global ADOM; live in the FortiWeb ADOM) (URL /reachability/)

What is it?#

Backend Reachability answers one question per line of a list: do the real servers behind this FortiWeb server policy answer — on the source appliance, and then on the destination appliance? It reads the pool members of each policy from each box and probes them. It needs no workspace tab or selected appliance, and it writes nothing: no clone, no migration, no configuration change.

Typical use: before or after migrating policies from one FortiWeb to another.

What does it do?#

  • Reads each line source;policy;destination (up to 200 lines).
  • On the source first, then the destination: reads the policy's pool members and probes each one.
  • Probes from two vantages, never merged:
  • this node — a TCP connection from SATOM to the member's port (always on; a refused port proves the host is up);
  • the appliance — execute ping over SSH from each box (optional).
  • Gives each line one verdict — error, down, mismatch, unknown, ok — plus every finding that earned it.
  • If the destination does not have the policy and SSH is on, the source's backends are pinged from the destination instead (the pre-migration question), and that side is labelled as such.
  • Reports anything it could not cover (time budget, target cap, over-limit lines) by name.
  • Copy TSV copies the report.

Requirements#

  • FortiWeb appliances registered in the current ADOM, reachable over their API.
  • For the appliance vantage: SSH credentials on the appliances.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Requires the legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example monitoring.view); all system profiles have it. Appliance names are resolved only among the appliances visible in the current ADOM. Each run is written to the audit log because it sends real traffic to third-party hosts.

How to use#

  1. Open Operations → Troubleshooting → Backend Reachability (Global ADOM or FortiWeb ADOM; until 2026-10-14 it sat under Operations → Troubleshooting in the FortiWeb ADOM).
  2. Under Lines to check, type or paste lines in One service per line, or use …or upload the file (.txt, .csv, .tsv, max 256 KB). An uploaded file replaces the box, and the box is refilled with it.
  3. Under Vantages, optionally tick Ask each appliance too (execute ping over SSH).
  4. Set TCP timeout (s) and Time budget (s) if needed.
  5. Click Check. Reset clears the page.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Lines source;policy;destination; # lines ignored; a two-field line (source;policy) checks the source only; a format header line is skipped Yes fweb-01;pol-shop;fweb-02
Ask each appliance too Adds the SSH execute ping vantage No off
TCP timeout (s) Per-connection timeout, 0.5–10 No 2
Time budget (s) Total run budget, 10–300 No 120

Appliance names are matched case-insensitively against appliance names first, then hosts. Only FortiWeb appliances are accepted.

Verdicts#

Verdict Typical findings
error malformed line, source/destination not found or unreadable, policy absent on the source, pool unreadable
down a member is unreachable
mismatch policy absent on the destination, member missing or extra on the destination, no pool, empty pool, all members disabled
unknown no vantage could probe, comparison skipped
ok every backend answered (a source-only line is complete when the source answers)

Example#

🧪Example — Pre-migration check of three services

# source;policy;destination
fweb-01;pol-shop;fweb-02
fweb-01;pol-api;fweb-02
fweb-02;pol-origin

With SSH on, line 1 is ok, line 2 is mismatch (destination lacks member 198.51.100.12:8443), line 3 is a source-only check.

Result#

  • The page shows the Report with line count, elapsed time, vantages, and per-verdict totals.
  • An audit entry reachability.batch records the number of lines, totals, whether SSH was used, elapsed time and whether the budget was hit.

Troubleshooting#

"nothing to check — one line per service, 'source;policy;destination'"#

The box was empty (or only comments). Enter at least one line.

"<file> is larger than 256 KB — this page takes a list of lines, not a config dump"#

Upload a smaller file.

"the file is not UTF-8 — it was read as latin-1, so check any line with accented characters"#

The file was decoded as latin-1. Check lines with accented characters.

"no appliance is registered as 'X' in this ADOM"#

The name does not match any visible appliance name or host. Check spelling or switch ADOM.

"X is a fortiadc — this check reads FortiWeb server policies"#

Only FortiWeb appliances can be named.

"over the 200-line limit for one run — split the file and run it again"#

Lines beyond 200 are listed as dropped. Split the file.

"This run did not cover everything it was given"#

The time budget or the target cap (2000 targets) was reached; the skipped lines/targets are named. Raise the Time budget (max 300 s) or split the list.

A member is "unknown" rather than down#

No vantage could probe it (for example SSH off and TCP inconclusive). A probe that could not run is never reported as an outage.

Advanced#

Advanced Behaviour details
  • Each appliance's API is read once per run, however many lines name it.
  • Probing is chunked (20 targets) so the budget is checked often.
  • Retired devices registered on a *.invalid host are refused before any connection is attempted.
  • Reading pool members and deciding reachability reuse the same logic as the post-clone backend probe, so both report the same verdict for the same backend.
#reachability#backend#pool members#ping#tcp probe#migration check#batch#source destination
